objective: Prove for laws on bits: a cycle of pairwise implications is a loop with one open distinction, and two such loops with one knot form the first-emergence structure; a law keeps a lasting record of loops exactly when it defines a parity knot, exactly when all its polymorphisms are affine; with constants this is exactly when local reasoning of bounded width fails; every hard law transmits; pairwise contradictions are shallow while parity charges are as deep as the layout's cut width; and an infinite pairwise cycle freezes its distinction while a parity network keeps every distinction finitely flippable.
status: Proved by BASE-THREE-20261021-001B-P001 (V1 prose proof with exhaustive and explicit checks; the ring theorem, the cutwidth and ends proofs, Post's lattice, Schaefer and Feder-Vardi cited). Pairwise implication cycles are loops (one open distinction), and two of them with one knot form the first-emergence structure that pairs alone never make. A law on bits keeps a lasting record of loops exactly when it defines parity, exactly when all its polymorphisms are affine, exactly when (with constants) no bounded local reasoning decides it. Pairwise and frozen laws are polynomial, so hardness lives inside transmission with memory; the transmitting regime splits into forcing (32 small laws), conservation (2) and choice (54, NP-complete with constants). Liar cycles are refuted at level 3; parity charges survive levels 2-4. An equality cycle fixes a distinction only a change of every member flips; a parity ring keeps every distinction flippable by three changes and hides one knot on all.
title: Proof: what the regimes carry
